relevance_note: Cohort of 13 patients with individual-level clinical and ALDH5A1 genotype tables: "Clinical features and ALDH5A1 gene findings in 13 Chinese cases with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency".
method_note: Built with a Python script in the scratch directory that split Table 1 and Table 2 rows into cells; every value was checked by me against the tables and text, and all spans were verified verbatim. Labels: Table 1/2 'Patient' column holds bare numbers, but the text uses 'Patient N' for every patient, so labels are 'Patient 1'..'Patient 13' (rule 1). Table 2 row '7 and 13' gives one genotype for both sibling sisters (Patients 7 and 13); both get those two variant rows. Table 2 second-allele rows have an empty Patient cell, so their spans are that row alone; Patient 4 and Patient 11 maternal c.1274T>C rows are textually identical. Inheritance: taken from Table 2 'Allele' column (Paternal/Maternal) for every patient; the text states parental sequencing only for patients 2, 7 and 11-13 (NGS 'and their parents'); for the others parental testing is not described, so the Allele column is the only basis. Zygosity left 'not reported': the paper never states heterozygous/compound heterozygous. Variant type only for the 12 novel variants the text classes by name; 'insertion' (c.206_222dup) and 'deletion' (c.85_116del) recorded as 'other'; previously reported variants left 'not reported'. Pathogenicity from the 'ACMG/AMP grading' column with the legend; ACMG criteria from the column headed 'ACMG classification'. Parents get no rows: no individual-level facts are given about any parent. Checklist: 'Psychomotor retardation' recorded as observed for gross or fine motor deficits (text: 'including delayed head-raising, sitting, and standing up' for all 13) but intellectual disability left not reported; language delay (8/13), epileptiform EEG (6 patients), lactate (8/10) are counts without names and exclude/assign no one. Table 1 listing of clinical features is not treated as exclusion of unlisted features. Paper's 'dystonia' (7 patients, 'characterized by hypotonia and/or paroxysmal hypertonia') is only assigned to Patient 8, whose row says dystonia. Patient 6 dentate-nucleus 'abnormal signals' is not stated as T2, so that checklist item is not reported for Patient 6. Patient 2 EEG 'suspected epileptic seizure' is hedged and not recorded. Emotional disturbance (Patients 6, 13) not mapped to depression or mood fluctuation. Normal liver/kidney function, electrolytes and full-term birth stated for 'all 13 patients' recorded as excluded abnormalities (group statement). Patient 2 last evaluation 'loss of follow up since 7 m' is ambiguous (age or interval), so no ISO given; Patient 9 likewise. Contradictions: (1) Patient 13: text 'presented with schizophrenia' / 'diagnosed as showing schizophrenia' vs Table 1 'misdiagnosed as “schizophrenia”' - both rows emitted, psychotic-symptoms checklist not reported. (2) Patient 11: Table 1 'suspected autism' vs text 'had autism spectrum disorder' - recorded observed with both spans. (3) Text says all 13 received taurine, but Table 1 main treatment omits taurine for Patients 2, 4, 7 and 9; treatment_summary uses the table cell. (4) Sleep disturbance without c.617del given as 66.7% (6/9) in Results and 60% (6/9) in Discussion. (5) c.617del vs 'c.617delT' in text; c.427del vs 'c.427delA' in abstract; c.1344-2del reference [7] for Patient 10 vs [6] for Patient 12. (6) EEG: 'performed in six patients', yet one + one + 'six patients' with spikes. (7) 'Eight patients underwent brain MRI' vs Discussion 'all patients' brain MRI scans showed different abnormalities'.
